text_devanagari: अ॒ना॒गसं॒ ब्रह्म॑णा त्वा कृणोमि शि॒वे ते॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी उ॒भे स्ता॑म् ॥ १ ॥
notes: Line begins with a left indent; no ink to the left of the first akshara in seg1. Marks written: 7 anudatta (a, na, sam, shi, te, thi, u) and 3 svarita (hma of brahmana, va of dyava, sta of stam). Vertical-band separation was clean: the middle line's headline sits at y~104 and its baseline at y~180 in both segments, so its anudatta bars fall in a tight band at y~205-225 (bar height ~10px) and its svarita strokes at y~68-100. A second band of horizontal bars sits at y~38-55 (seg1 x~492-528, 601-637, 821-858; seg2 x~117-152, 253-300, 317-351, 488-535, 748-784, 1119-1152); these are ~140px above the middle line's baseline, i.e. one full line-pitch too high, so they are anudatta of the line ABOVE and were NOT transcribed. Two sub-baseline marks were rejected as vowel signs, not accents: seg1 x1194-1236 (height 21px, hooked) is the vocalic r of कृ, and seg2 x625-666 (height 33px, hooked) is the vocalic r of पृ; both are visibly hooks, not the ~10px horizontal dashes of the anudatta. The dot at seg1 x644-663 above स is the anusvara of सं, not a svarita. Svarita placement is self-consistent in this fount: the stroke sits over the right edge of the base consonant, before any following aa-matra; in स्ता॑म् the stroke (x1163-1171) is ~30px left of the aa-vertical (x1200-1214) and detached from it, so the akshara is ता with a svarita, not तो. First akshara read as अ per the 1856 fount (looks like ऋ/श्र to a modern eye). Segments overlap by 91px (seg1 x = seg2 x + 1477), verified by an exact column-profile match, so no material falls between them. No mark was left unattributed.
